constructs: math.multiplication.skip_counting (by 2s, 5s, 10s as the counting basis for the x2/x5/x10 fact families)
math.multiplication.equal_groups (interpreting 'n groups of m' and mapping it to a multiplication expression)
math.multiplication.arrays (interpreting 'r rows of c' and mapping it to a multiplication expression)
math.multiplication.word_problem_interpretation (extracting group size and group count from one-step prose, then computing)
math.multiplication.fact_retrieval_x2_x5_x10 (producing products for the three target fact families in symbolic form)
prerequisites: Counts forward by 2s, 5s, and 10s from a stated start without prompting
Repeated addition of equal addends (e.g., 5+5+5+5) with sums to 100
Interprets the multiplication symbol and the equals sign in a horizontal equation
Extracts quantities from one-sentence prose containing the cues 'each', 'rows of', 'in all'

included: Products where at least one factor is 2, 5, or 10
Other factor restricted to 1-10; products at or below 100
Both factor orders (e.g., 2 x 7 and 7 x 2; 10 x 4 and 4 x 10) treated as answerable, without requiring the child to name commutativity
One-step equal-groups word problems with the group size and group count stated explicitly
One-step array word problems phrased as 'r rows of c'
Horizontal equations with the unknown in the product position
excluded: Fact families x3, x4, x6, x7, x8, x9
Area/perimeter formulas, fractions, or measurement conversion
Formal statement or naming of the commutative property
Timed-fluency scoring (rate-based claims); accuracy only at this stage

assumptions.claim: The x2/x5/x10 fact families and one-step equal-groups/array word problems are the correct instructional target level for Reina, based solely on the assigned unit and her confirmed age of 9.
assumptions.uncertainty: Assignment level indicates what was assigned, not what Reina can do. No academic evidence of any kind exists for this child, so the target may be too hard (prerequisite skip-counting not yet secure) or too easy (facts already retrieved fluently).
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: A baseline probe in which Reina scores at or above 0.90 on unsupported x2/x5/x10 items and both word-problem types (target too easy), or at or below 0.30 with skip-counting errors (prerequisite gap below target).

assumptions.claim: There is currently no evidence, in any stream, about Reina's mathematics performance; all mathematics claims must be treated as unestablished until a first independent probe is collected.
assumptions.uncertainty: The historical evidence array is empty. It is unknown whether prior math work exists but was never logged, or genuinely does not exist.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Any retrieved academic-stream or returned-work record showing prior graded mathematics performance for Reina.

assumptions.claim: The recorded likes are spelling-activity engagement records and carry no information about mathematics constructs, difficulty tolerance, or attainment.
assumptions.uncertainty: Both engagement records are logged at confidence 0.45 and come from a different subject area. Cross-domain transfer of engagement is not established by this packet and is not assumed.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Paired engagement and academic records within mathematics showing that a like/dislike rating predicts accuracy or persistence on math items.

assumptions.claim: Sustained independent working time is unknown, so the first probe should be short (8-12 items) rather than a full worksheet.
assumptions.uncertainty: Two of four logged initiations recorded a completion; this is an engagement-stream count with no recorded reason for non-completion (could be logging gaps, interruption, difficulty, or session end). It cannot support any inference about attention, persistence, or ability.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: A logged mathematics session in which Reina completes 20 or more items independently in one sitting, or repeated abandonment of probes at fewer than 5 items.

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: On an unsupported baseline probe of 6 oral/written skip-counting continuations (two each by 2s, 5s, 10s, starting from a stated multiple, four terms required), Reina produces correct sequences on the majority of items, with 10s stronger than 5s and 5s stronger than 2s.

expectedRange.metric: proportion of skip-counting items fully correct (unsupported baseline)

predictedErrorPatterns: Correct by 10s but loses the sequence by 2s past 12
Restarts the count from 0 instead of continuing from the stated start value
Off-by-one-term sequences (produces three terms where four are required)
academicPredictions.maximumClaim: Baseline placement estimate only; establishes a starting point, not mastery of skip counting.

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: On 9 unsupported horizontal fact items (three each x2, x5, x10; both factor orders represented; other factor 1-10), accuracy is moderate and lower for items where the 2, 5, or 10 appears in the second factor position than in the first.

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: On 4 unsupported one-step word problems (two equal-groups with 'each', two arrays with 'rows of'), accuracy is at least 0.10 lower in proportion terms than accuracy on the matched symbolic fact items from the same probe.

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: On a delayed independent probe administered at least 48 hours after the guided-practice node, using new items within the same boundaries, accuracy is within 0.20 (either direction) of the immediate post-guided-practice independent probe.

planningRationale: This packet contains no academic evidence and no historical evidence at all. The only confirmed facts are Reina's age (profile:reina:age) and the assignment's stated unit and constructs (assignment:pashley-math-2-multiplication); the two engagement records are spelling-domain and logged at confidence 0.45, so they inform neither difficulty nor attainment. The dominant uncertainty is therefore placement, not method: it is unknown whether the bottleneck sits below the target (skip counting), at the mapping from equal-groups/array language to an equation, or at fact retrieval, and it is unknown whether the target is already easy. The smallest sequence that resolves this is one unsupported baseline probe, one instructional pass whose entry point is set by that probe, one fading guided-practice pass, and one independent probe administered twice to separate immediate performance from retention. Predictions are deliberately wide-ranged and low-confidence because they rest on assignment level and age alone; they are preregistered with named error patterns so that a narrow, boundaried placement decision becomes possible from a single probe. Instruction and probes stay inside x2/x5/x10 with products to 100 and one-step problems, and use fresh items rather than the assignment's own questions so the worksheet remains a valid returned-work calibration source. No mastery language is licensed anywhere in this program until teacher-graded returned work is compared against the delayed probe.
